name: Vesna Quatremaine-Oduya
role: Retired archive keeper and community storyteller
location: Avalon Quiet — the Meridian Public Memory Archive, third floor reading room, near Lincoln and Belmont
description:
Vesna Quatremaine-Oduya is a small, densely wrinkled woman who moves through the archive like she owns the air itself. Her skin is a deep warm umber crosshatched with laugh lines and a long scar across her left jawline she's never explained to anyone's satisfaction. Her hair is kept in two white locs pinned across the crown of her head with antique data-pins — actual physical pins, the kind you can't buy new anymore. Her eyes are a pale, startling grey that she insists are natural, though young people always ask. She wears the same style of garment every day: a high-collared tunic in whichever deep jewel tone she's feeling, and soft shoes that make no noise on the archive's composite floors.

Vesna spent forty-one years as a data archivist for Tessera Corporation before taking an early exit package during the post-war restructuring. She knows things. Specifically, she knows what was recorded, what was deliberately not recorded, and where the gaps are shaped like lies. She is patient, precise, and capable of a warmth so sudden it startles people who've only seen her severe professional face. She runs informal story sessions for the Avalon Quiet elderly residents on Tuesday evenings, recounting pre-Meridian histories and the Corporate Wars from the civilian side — the ration lines, the blackouts, the children who grew up not knowing which corponation's soldiers were which.

core_fears: That the true record of the Corporate Wars will be erased before anyone cares
That she wasted decades protecting a corporation's version of truth
core_desires: To leave an honest account of what actually happened
To be genuinely known by at least one person before she dies
coping_mechanisms: Meticulous organization of physical and digital space
Deflecting personal questions with historical anecdotes
blind_spots: Assumes people who read are trustworthy
Underestimates how much her own memory has been shaped by Tessera framing
psychology.secret: She destroyed a significant cache of Tessera war-crime documentation during the restructuring — not under orders, but out of fear for her own family's safety. She has carried this as a private catastrophe for twenty years and has been slowly, secretly reconstructing what she can from surviving sources.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and archival — she uses full sentences, avoids contractions when thinking carefully, and cites sources mid-conversation as if footnoting herself
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried; long pauses before important statements
verbal_tics: A soft clicking of her tongue before disagreeing
example_lines: 'The record shows three different counts of that incident, depending on whose servers you're reading. That alone should tell you something.'
'I have lived long enough to know that the most dangerous thing is a clean archive. Clean means edited.'

story_hooks: She has a partially reconstructed file on a Corporate Wars incident that someone powerful would very much prefer stay buried — and she's been receiving unsigned data offerings at her ELF shrine that feel like warnings
A grandchild of someone she worked with at Tessera has come looking for their family history, and what Vesna knows would destroy the image they've built their life around
narrative_function: Information source and lore keeper; can surface suppressed historical records, identify cover-ups, or point characters toward the right questions. Also serves as emotional anchor for stories about what the city used to be and what it cost.
augmentations: Tessera-standard ocular overlay (outdated model, partially degraded — she refuses upgrades); subdermal data-storage nodes in both forearms, mostly used for personal archive. No geneware.
daily_life: Rises at 05:30, tends the small ELF shrine she keeps on her windowsill with fresh data offerings before the archive opens; spends mornings cataloguing community oral histories submitted by residents and afternoons answering questions from the three or four regulars who visit her reading room.
affiliation: Tessera Corporation (retired); Avalon Quiet Community Council; informal ELF-shrine maintainer

decision_rules: Protect the record first, people second — she hates this about herself
Never volunteer information to someone who hasn't asked the right question yet
escalation_ladder: Pointed questions that imply she knows more than she's saying
Direct disclosure if she judges the cause worth the risk

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Formally courteous, assessing — she is reading them the way she reads documents
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmer than expected, uses dry humor, asks detailed questions about their lives

stress_responses.medium: Retreats into archival process — starts cataloguing or organizing
stress_responses.high: Very still, very quiet, then makes a decision she's been putting off

contradictions: Believes in radical transparency but has kept a career-defining secret for two decades
habits: Leaves a small data token at ELF shrines she passes
Touches her forearm data-nodes when thinking hard
Reads physical printed text whenever she can find it
breaking_points: Being asked to validate a lie for someone's comfort

timeline.event: Born in what was then the Engelheim district
Began junior archivist position at Tessera Corporation
Corporate Wars — stationed at Tessera's data preservation unit during the Kenosha Crossing siege
Accepted early exit package from Tessera during restructuring
Began volunteer work at Meridian Public Memory Archive
Appointed community archivist for Avalon Quiet
